data.title: Bloom Energy Supports Central Texas First Responders Ahead of Florida-Texas Matchup
data.description:
Bloom Energy () continued its season-long partnership with ESPN Radio’s College Football Campus Tour this week in Austin, Texas.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261016766768/en/

Ahead of the Florida-Texas matchup, Bloom visited Austin Fire Department Station #3 and presented a $10,000 donation to the Central Texas Public Safety Commission, a nonprofit organization that supports police, fire and EMS departments across Central Texas.

For more than 25 years, the Central Texas Public Safety Commission has worked with first responders and community partners to identify and fund critical needs, including equipment, training, wellness programs and community initiatives that strengthen public safety.

“Every community’s resilience ultimately depends on people,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “The firefighters, EMS personnel and first responders supported by the Central Texas Public Safety Commission are the people communities turn to on their hardest days. We are proud to support an organization that helps ensure they have the resources they need to serve Central Texas.”

“The Central Texas Public Safety Commission provides critical support for equipment, training and other needs that fall outside our normal operating budget,” said Austin Interim Fire Chief Tom Vocke. “Support from organizations like Bloom Energy helps supplement city resources and ensures our firefighters have what they need to stay safe and ready to respond.”

Austin Fire Department Station #3 opened in 1957 and serves the University of Texas and surrounding Central Austin neighborhoods. The station reopened in October 2023 following a renovation that rebuilt its apparatus bays and added dedicated spaces designed to improve firefighter health and safety while preserving the station’s original design.

Bloom will also be on the University of Texas campus Saturday during pregame festivities, where fans can take part in an interactive experience and learn more about Bloom's work, providing clean, reliable power for essential services and critical infrastructure across the country.

Upcoming Confirmed 2026 Tour Stops

  • October 17 – Austin, Texas | Florida at Texas

  • November 7 – Oxford, Mississippi | Georgia at Ole Miss

  • November 14 – Baton Rouge, Louisiana | Texas at LSU

  • November 21 – Lincoln, Nebraska | Ohio State at Nebraska

  • November 28 – Nashville, Tennessee | Tennessee at Vanderbilt

About Bloom Energy

Bloom Energy empowers enterprises to meet soaring energy demands and responsibly take charge of their power needs. The company’s fuel cell systems provide ultra-reliable, clean and highly scalable onsite electricity for Fortune 500 customers around the world, including data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, large utilities and other commercial and industrial sectors, as well as mission-critical organizations in local communities, such as hospitals, college campuses and retailers. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, Bloom Energy employs more than 2,000 people worldwide and manufactures its systems in the United States. For more information, visit BloomEnergy.com.

WaFd reported fiscal year 2026 net income of $255.9 million and diluted earnings per common share of $3.21, a 22% increase in EPS year-over-year. For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, WaFd recorded net income of $59.99 million and diluted EPS of $0.76. Financial Highlights

  • Fiscal year 2026 net income: $255,865,000.
  • Fiscal year 2026 diluted earnings per common share: $3.21 (22% increase vs. prior year $2.63).
  • Quarter (Q4 FY2026) net income: $59,991,000; diluted EPS: $0.76.
  • Net interest income for Q4: $182.4 million; net interest margin: 2.81%.
  • Q4 non-interest income: $38.1 million (including $16.4 million gain on sale of single-family loans); Q4 non-interest expense: $121.5 million; efficiency ratio: 55.12%.

Business Highlights

  • Total assets increased to $27.2 billion as of September 30, 2026, driven by $1.4 billion of investment securities purchases focused on discount-priced 30-year mortgage-backed securities.
  • Transaction deposits grew 4.6% year-over-year; transaction accounts comprised 60.4% of deposits as of September 30, 2026.
  • Net loans decreased to $19.04 billion due to loan-sale activity, including $543 million of single-family residential loan sales in Q4 and an agreement to sell $429 million of multifamily loans classified as held for sale.
  • Active loan originations totaled $5.5 billion for fiscal 2026 (95% commercial, 5% consumer); repayments offset originations with $3.9 billion in repayments during the year.
  • Asset quality improved following resolution of a $53 million loan relationship (resulting in a $36 million charge-off); non-performing assets and delinquencies decreased materially to 0.32% of total assets and 0.50% of total loans, respectively, as of September 30, 2026.

data.title: Coca-Cola, Visa and Mastercard Hit Records as Investors Rotate Out of Chip Stocks — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Paul R. La Monica

Chip stocks have fizzled, but investors are finding fresh highs outside tech. Call it the revenge of the old economy.

Coca-Cola, a quintessential consumer staples stock and longtime favorite of Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway, hit a new all-time high this week. So did Visa and Mastercard, two top financials, as well as life insurance leader MetLife.

Over in the oil patch, Chevron, Shell and ConocoPhillips notched new all-time highs on Friday. Healthcare stocks Gilead Sciences, Thermo Fisher Scientific and McKesson recently hit record highs as well, as did consumer discretionary stocks Urban Outfitters, Williams-Sonoma and SharkNinja. (Chevron, Visa, Gilead Sciences and SharkNinja are all recent Barron's stock picks.)

What's missing? Tech — for the most part. Apple isn't far from a new all-time high. But the shift away from momentum-driven chip stocks, which were surging thanks to expectations of even more big spending on AI by the top hyperscalers, is a sign that investors are largely shrugging off the sector's slump. Chip stocks were on pace Friday to extend their losing streak to nine straight sessions.

"Rotation continues to be the theme," said Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading, in a report Thursday. O'Rourke has been vocal about how concentrated the market is but added in his report that it is encouraging to see that the S&P 500 isn't far from its record high despite the notable pullback in chip stocks.

Third-quarter earnings season, which kicked off in earnest this week with several reports from big banks and is set to continue next week with GE Aerospace, Netflix, Meta Platforms, Tesla and Procter & Gamble among the megacap highlights, could be another catalyst for a continued broadening of the rally.

Nicole Inui, head of equity strategy for the Americas at HSBC, said in a report that "unloved sectors," such as financials, and consumer discretionary and real estate could get a lift if companies report better-than-expected earnings and offer upbeat guidance.

"U.S. economic activity continues to hold up better than expected," Inui added. "Earnings leadership could broaden. That, in turn, would support wider participation in the market and an improvement in index breadth."

Valuations also appear reasonable enough to spark a broader rally if earnings for companies outside tech and AI come in stronger than expected. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF is trading for less than 16 times earnings estimates for the next 12 months, a bigger-than-usual discount to the cap-weighted index.

"Robust earnings growth has remained widespread across the market this year and is even accelerating, which are facts investors may not fully appreciate," said Mike Dickson, head of research at Horizon, in a recent report.

"As earnings come in over the next several weeks, many market sectors may perk up and join the rally. With many stocks below their highs, continued strong earnings growth across sectors could lift more stocks and help the broader market rise in the coming months," Dickson added.

So investors who may be licking their wounds from the recent selloff in chip stocks should take some comfort from the fact that the rest of the market is starting to pick up the slack for semiconductors.

Write to Paul R. La Monica at paul.lamonica@barrons.com

data.title: Nasdaq Plunges To One-Month Low Amid Renewed Tech Sell-Off
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After recovering from an early slump to end Thursday's session mostly higher, stocks showed a significant move back to the downside during trading on Friday. Technology stocks led the way lower, dragging the tech-heavy Nasdaq down to its lowest closing level in a month.

The Nasdaq ended the day off its lows of the session but still plunged 572.99 points or 2.1 percent to 26,140.03. The S&P 500 also slumped 84.62 points or 1.1 percent to 7,659.44, while the narrower Dow posted a more modest loss, falling 175.28 points or 0.3 percent to 52,002.41.

For the week, the Nasdaq plummeted by 4.5 percent and the S&P 500 tumbled by 2 percent, but the Dow increased by 0.7 percent.

A renewed sell-off among technology stocks weighed on the Nasdaq amid concerns about debt-fueled AI infrastructure spending.

Computer hardware stocks turned in some of the tech sector's worst performances, extending the nosedive seen over the past couple weeks, with the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index plummeting by 5.4 percent to a two-month closing low.

Semiconductor, networking and software also saw substantial weakness, contributing to the steep drop by the Nasdaq.

Outside of the tech sector, airline stocks moved sharply lower amid an extended surge by the price of crude oil, dragging the NYSE Arca Airline Index down by 3.2 percent.

Brokerage and biotechnology stocks also saw notable weakness, while energy stocks moved significantly higher along with the price of crude oil.

U.S. crude oil futures spiked back above $100 a barrel for the first time in a month as Iran has re-escalated its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the purported 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine has seemingly unraveled.

On the U.S. economic front, a report released by the Federal Reserve showed industrial production in the U.S. increased by more than expected in the month of September.

The Fed said industrial production climbed by 0.7 percent in September following a revised 0.1 percent uptick in August.

Economists had expected industrial production to rise by 0.4 percent compared to the unchanged reading originally reported for the previous month.

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly higher during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index shot up by 1.4 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index increased by 0.5 percent.

The major European markets have moved to the upside on the day. While the German DAX Index jumped by 1 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index climbed by 0.4 percent and the French CAC 40 Index rose by 0.3 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have shown a lack of direction following a recent rally. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its, is down by 1.2 basis points at 5.075 percent.

data.title: SpaceX Stocks Fall 1.94% Despite Evercore's $275 Price Target
data.description:
Space, connectivity and AI company SpaceX traded at $145.73, down 1.94%, at 11:35 a.m. ET on October 16, despite a bigger price target from Evercore ISI. According to Investing.com, the firm maintained its Outperform rating and raised its target to $275 from $230. That is a 19.6% increase in the target. The investment case now carries a higher bar for execution.

Evercore increased its 2027 computing-capacity estimate to 6.5 gigawatts from 5.7 gigawatts, a roughly 14% revision, according to the report. Separately, SpaceX's September 28 mission account says Starship Flight 14 deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Those developments measure different things. A successful satellite deployment marks progress for connectivity, but it does not establish that projected computing capacity will be financed, powered and delivered on schedule.

The valuation leaves little room for easy assumptions. The financial snapshot shows a $1.98 trillion market capitalization, a 15.09 price-to-book ratio and a GF Score of just 15 out of 100a combination that puts pressure on future execution to justify the price. Investors need evidence that computing projects can become operating capacity and that satellite deployments can generate paying usage. A higher analyst target lifts expectations. Turning those expectations into durable cash flow is the harder job.

data.title: Compass sues California's listing service over anti-competitive rules - report
data.description:
Compass has sued the California Regional Multiple Listing Service for allegedly adopting anti-competitive rules, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

The federal court suit filed in Los Angeles reportedly alleges that CRMLS's requirement that agents list homes for sale within one business day or face fines violates U.S. antitrust laws, according to the report.

CRMLS is "dictating how Compass and its agents can and cannot compete, how Compass and its agents can and cannot serve their clients, and how homeowners can and cannot market their own homes," the company reportedly said.

The listing service had sued Compass earlier this month in New York, seeking a court order in support of its listings rules. According to the listing service, Compass wants to publicly advertise homes on its platform while withholding those same listings from the shared database, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Intel Stocks Fall 3.9% as TSMC's Packaging Comments Challenge Its Expansion
data.description:
Intel, the processor and chip manufacturing group , faces fresh advanced-packaging competition, with shares at $91.61, down approximately 3.94%, at 11:17 a.m. ET on October 16. According to TipRanks, TSMC has signaled it can support customers if competing packaging capacity falls short. That raises the stakes for Intel's expansion. It does not establish that Intel has lost a customer or an order.

TSMC's earnings transcript outlines its packaging technology ambitions, underscoring the pressure Intel faces to deliver at scale. Intel's own numbers show why execution matters: its second-quarter results recorded $5.765 billion in Foundry revenue and a $2.089 billion operating loss. That puts the loss at roughly 36.2% of segment revenue. Revenue includes internal transactions, and those figures cover the broader Foundry business rather than packaging alone. Winning work is one hurdle. Making it profitable is another.

The valuation leaves little room for disappointment: Intel's $91.61 share price stands 182.92% above its $32.38 GF Value estimate. That premium suggests investors are already paying for substantial improvement, even while Foundry remains deeply unprofitable. The next test is concrete: deliver packaging milestones, convert demand into production and narrow the losses. Technology progress matters, but stronger factory economics would give the turnaround more financial weight.

data.title: Memory Chip Stocks Crashed 50% -- BofA Delivers Powerful Warning to Bears
data.description:
Bank of America sees the retreat in memory-chip shares as sharper than the industry's outlook warrants, and expects pricing and margins to remain supportive through 2028.

SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) have each lost more than 50% from June peaks. Yet based on projected 2027 and 2028 earnings, both trade at two to three times earnings, below multiples of four to seven times seen in previous memory upcycles.

BofA expects memory prices, sales and profitability to hold up over the next two years. Although 2028 earnings per share could ease by a single-digit percentage, analysts expect profits to remain near record levels.

Investors are watching SK Hynix's Oct. 28 outlook for the December quarter, which could include a special cash dividend. Taiwan's Nanya Technology has already issued a positive forecast. BofA also cited monthly PC memory contract-price increases of at least 15% and steady spot prices.

Investor views remain divided. Concerns include financing pressures among AI cloud providers, additional Chinese supply and slower AI spending, even as the bank sees fundamentals supporting the sector.
